transcript.content: Hi, I'm Dr. [Name]. Welcome in—what brings you here to see me today?

Well, I came in because... honestly, I feel like I’m just falling apart. They recently changed my hours at the warehouse and put in this new inventory system, and ever since then, things have just been really bad. 

I’m missing shifts at work, missing my church commitments... I've been snapping at my family, too, which isn't like me. Some mornings I just sit there on the edge of the bed in my work boots, just wondering if I can even face the place anymore. It's just getting to be too much.
When exactly did you start feeling this way—how long has it been since the new hours and inventory system started?

It's been about five months now. Yeah, right around five months ago is when they rolled out the new schedule and that inventory system at the warehouse. I've been feeling like this pretty much ever since it started.
Over these past five months, have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy, nearly every day for most of the day?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or down like that. Not every day, anyway. I mean, I'm just incredibly stressed and overwhelmed by the whole situation at work. 

It's not that I've lost interest in the things I normally enjoy... I just feel too wound up or exhausted from dealing with the warehouse to actually do them right now. But no, I don't just sit around feeling sad all day.
Aside from the stress about work, do you find yourself excessively worrying about other things in your life—like your health, finances, or family—that feels hard to control?

No, not really. I mean, my health is fine for my age, and I'm not losing sleep over my finances or my family or anything like that. 

It's really just the job. The warehouse and that new system... that's what's got me all tied up in knots. If it weren't for what's going on at work, I wouldn't be worrying like this. It all just comes back to that.
When you think about going to work or dealing with the new system, do you notice physical signs of anxiety—like a racing heart, muscle tension, or feeling on edge—along with the stress?

Not really, no. I mean, my heart doesn't race or anything like that. I definitely feel on edge just thinking about having to go in and use that system, but... it's not really a physical feeling for me. I don't have muscle tension or whatever. It's just a constant, heavy stress in my mind.
When you're sitting there in the morning feeling like that, do you ever have thoughts of hurting yourself or wishing you weren't around?

No, no, nothing like that. I don't want to hurt myself. I just... I just don't want to deal with that computer system. But I'm not wishing I was dead or anything. I just want to do my job the way I've always done it.
